solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cleric keeps company with shrewd colleague

definitions.note: self-referential: the answer is a colleague of the cleric in the wordplay

parts.note: arch means knowing or cunning

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman in charge of a cathedral
the standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A priest spends his time alongside a sharp-witted workmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleric' looks like the definition but belongs to the wordplay; the definition is 'colleague', which only makes sense by reference to that cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican clergyman who works alongside the dean in a diocese, so a fellow churchman.

clue.text: Passionate, vocal woman who leads uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upwards, turning the letters back to front

parts.note: a diva is a leading female singer, a prima donna

explanation.surface: A fiery female singer heads a popular revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vocal woman who leads' describes a prima donna, the lead singer of an opera company.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone with keen, eager enthusiasm for something, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Start to cause trouble about final piece of work

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of cause

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: Someone begins making a fuss about the last part of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a troublemaker at work; 'work' is really a musical or literary work.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a musical composition or the closing section of a book or play.

clue.text: Left with no illusions after he sent candid snaps

indicators.note: something that snaps breaks apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was abandoned and disillusioned after a man shared revealing photos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snaps' looks like photographs, the object of 'sent'; it is the verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disenchanted means having lost one's former faith or illusions, the spell of admiration broken.

clue.text: Cycling bore gets fit

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round, so the first letter goes round to the back

parts.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: A tedious cyclist gets into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as a dull person but is a tidal wave up an estuary, called an EAGRE; moving its first letter to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that fit together correspond or match, just as figures or accounts that agree tally with one another.

clue.text: Fail to rise to the occasion when one should?

definitions.text: Fail to rise to the occasion when one should?

parts.words: Fail to rise to the occasion
parts.note: surface reading: to fall short when a challenge comes
setter's reading: literally not getting out of bed at the time you ought to

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom about meeting a challenge is taken literally: to rise here means to get up in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping past the intended waking time means not getting out of bed when planned.

clue.text: Part company with surgery led by GP?

indicators.note: what is led by something comes after it, fixing which piece goes first

parts.note: a GP (general practitioner) is a doctor, abbreviated DR
OP is short for operation

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a medical practice that is run by a family doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surgery' suggests a GP's premises, as it does in Britain, but here it is an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a friend or associate is to end the relationship and stop seeing them.

clue.text: Leaders of right-wing establishment host US counterpart

indicators.note: leaders stand at the front, so only the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words
a publican is the landlord who hosts a pub

explanation.surface: Heads of a conservative institution entertain their American equivalent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: the American counterpart of a British right-winger is a member of the GOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republican Party is the main conservative party in America, the equivalent of Britain's Tories.

clue.text: Having prominent corporation with pounds in bank misrepresented

parts.note: the pot is the pool of money staked in a card game, the bank

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to belie is to give a false impression of
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A big company with money in the bank has been misrepresented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old humorous word for a large belly, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a sticking-out paunch is described as having a large round stomach like a cooking pot.

clue.text: Liable to produce spoilers maybe from popular record about film

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: in means fashionable
a disc is a record
re means concerning
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A hit record about a film might give away the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is the old commercial 'concerning', used as a charade piece here rather than a signal; spoilers are plot secrets let slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives away plot twists is careless about keeping secrets, one example of tactless talk.

clue.text: Words expressed with venom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quarrel, as in having words with someone
second meaning: said angrily, the past tense of spit

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about bitter speech; split it, and 'words' is a noun for an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor row is a noun sense, and the past tense of the verb meaning to utter furiously is the other.

clue.text: A banal tune — it swings like The Impossible Dream?

indicators.note: something that swings moves about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A trite melody has the swing of a famous show tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The Impossible Dream is the big song from the musical Man of La Mancha, about reaching the unreachable star.
explanation.definitionFit: An impossible dream by its nature can never be reached or achieved, however hard one tries.

clue.text: Ill-timed, immoderate needs succeeded for king

indicators.note: one thing given for another is exchanged for it, a straight swap of letters

parts.note: unreasonable means excessive
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Someone's excessive demands followed a king's reign at a bad moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of UNREASONABLE is swapped for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseasonable weather comes at the wrong time of year, so the word means badly timed or inopportune.

clue.text: Base of lower lip harbours what appears to be rash

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so one piece holds another

parts.note: lip is cheek, insolence

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, the final letter of a word

parts.note: the final letter of lower

explanation.surface: A mark under the bottom lip seems to be a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning reckless; 'what appears to be rash' is behaviour that shows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is lack of caution, the quality shown by hasty, reckless behaviour.

clue.text: Swims at speed in shallow area with access to facilities

definitions.text: shallow area with access to facilities

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke
pace is rate of movement

explanation.surface: Someone swims fast in the shallow end of a pool with changing rooms nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimming-pool picture of a shallow end and facilities is really about wiring and pipes under a house.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a low gap under a floor or roof, too shallow to stand in, giving access to pipes and wiring.

clue.text: Walk then run, being in a frenzied state

parts.note: to march is to walk briskly
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Someone walks and then runs while in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as a verb but is a noun, a creature; 'mad as a March hare' is the saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Hares in the spring breeding season behave wildly, boxing and leaping, hence the proverbial madness of this animal.

clue.text: Pay for issue brought up previously

parts.note: to atone for a wrong is to make amends

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means lifting from the bottom, so the letters read in the other direction

parts.note: to emit is to give out

explanation.surface: Someone paid for a matter raised earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue brought up' suggests a topic raised in discussion; 'issue' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means formerly, in the past, on some earlier occasion.

clue.text: Test case for tribunal involves revolutionary aspect

indicators.note: to involve is to enfold or include, so one piece sits within another
a case is the outer shell, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an air is a manner or appearance

explanation.surface: A landmark court case raises a radical point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test case' wants to be one phrase and the definition; the definition is 'Test' alone, and 'case for tribunal' is its outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is an experiment or tryout of something, the same as a test of it.

clue.text: Large plant finishes off reactor to allow extra production

indicators.note: a finish is the end, so only the final letters are taken

parts.note: the last letters of five words

explanation.surface: A big power station completes its reactor so it can make more output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large plant' suggests a factory or power station; it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree, and trees are large woody plants.

clue.text: Children's home forever faced by endless changes

indicators.note: to be faced by is to have something in front, fixing the order
without ends means dropping both the first and last letters, keeping the middle

parts.note: morphs means changes form; without its ends it loses M and S
an age is an extremely long time

explanation.surface: A home for children stays the same forever while things endlessly change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children's' looks like part of the wordplay's scene; the definition is the whole phrase. 'Forever' gives the two words AN AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is a residential institution caring for young people without parents.

clue.text: Male characters in The Devils spread confusion

indicators.note: to spread is to scatter, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: men are male people
taken as written

explanation.surface: The men in The Devils sow chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The Devils suggests the Ken Russell film or Dostoevsky novel, but its letters are simply combined with MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishevelment is untidiness or disorder, a state of muddle, so it matches a mess or disarray.

clue.text: What features in chironomid genetically?

indicators.note: whatever features in a phrase is part of it, so the letters sit within the words

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: What shows up in the DNA of a particular insect?
explanation.walkthrough: Chironomids are a family of small flies; the answer runs across the end of one word and start of the next, and the whole clue defines it too.
explanation.definitionFit: A chironomid is a non-biting fly of the family Chironomidae, commonly called a midge, so it is genetically one.

clue.text: Small drop in attendance initially disrupting teacher's course

indicators.note: to disrupt is to break into, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of attendance

explanation.surface: A slight fall in numbers upsets a teacher's class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small drop' reads as a decline in attendance; it is a droplet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead of sweat or dew is a small round droplet of liquid.

clue.text: Staunch supporter of green growth?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
second meaning: the stalk holding up leaves and flowers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch supporter' reads as a loyal backer of environmental policy; 'Staunch' is a separate verb, and the green growth is foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check it, and a plant's main stalk holds up its leaves.

clue.text: Close listener follows note

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, fixing which piece goes second

parts.note: N is short for note
the ear is what listens

explanation.surface: An attentive listener pays heed to a written message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close listener' reads as one attentive person; 'Close' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Near and close both mean at a short distance away, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Writer set out to capture live animal

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: An author set off to catch a creature alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' reads as setting off on a trip; 'set' is the fodder and 'out' the signal, and the writer plus the rearranged letters together hold BE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest, or gnu, is a large African antelope, a hoofed mammal of the savannah.

clue.text: Square divisible by two

definitions.meaning: first meaning: level, all debts settled, as in being square with someone
second meaning: the mathematical term for such a number

explanation.walkthrough: Square numbers suggest mathematics, which the second meaning continues, but 'Square' here means quits.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits with nobody owing anything is one sense; an integer with no remainder when halved is the other.

clue.text: Poll's official objective hedged by expressions of doubt

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official

indicators.note: something hedged by others is fenced in, so it sits between them

parts.note: er and um are hesitant noises
an end is an aim

explanation.surface: An election's stated aim is surrounded by uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' reads as an adjective meaning impartial, fitting an official, but it is a noun meaning a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a vote by the whole electorate on a single question, a type of ballot.
